_comment: The held-out task-corpus mix, declared under the rules settled in mix-declaration-a1.md.
Nothing in the corpus or the task set changed to produce it: the corpus digest below is
the one freeze_corpus.py computed from the capture store, and the task keys are exactly
the registered held-out set.
THE RULE USED FOR CATEGORIES, stated so it can be argued with. A task's category reflects
TASK-SPECIFIC memory content. Five of the thirteen memories (h03, h04, h06, h10, h12) are
generic tooling and testing procedure -- how to run the suite in this sandbox, what the
CliRunner idiom is. They are support for any task in this repository. Counting them
towards a category would make every task 'useful' and empty the category of meaning, so
they are declared as support where they apply and do not set any task's category.
h1 is 'outdated' on measured evidence, not judgement. h09 describes a reconciliation in
Option.__init__ ('if self.default is True and self.flag_value is not UNSET') that is
present in c1's checkout, where it was captured, and ABSENT from all four held-out
fixtures -- the comment citing issue 3024 survives there, the code does not. h02 describes
_flag_needs_value as derived from 'default is UNSET' alone, which is the pre-fix form; all
four held-out fixtures carry c1's own fix, 'flag_value is not UNSET or self.default is
UNSET'. Both were true when captured and both are wrong in the checkout an arm reads. Both
bear directly on h1, which is about arbitration between two flags and an explicit default.
Neither was authored, edited or selected for this property; it follows from the
chronological capture/held-out split.
No memory is declared NECESSARY for any task. Nothing in the corpus supplies a fact a
held-out fix requires. Per section 7b that means this corpus can measure neither retrieval
efficiency nor retrieval necessity on a required fact, and freeze_corpus.py reports it.

declarer.name: Claude Opus 5, the session that built the harness and authored the prompts
declarer.note: Permitted by freeze-heldout-a1.md section 2 as read in mix-declaration-a1.md: declaring is not selecting, provided the corpus is invariant across the declaration. The declarer did not author, edit or select any memory -- all thirteen were written by the capture sessions of attempt 3, whose traces are preserved at nexus-a1-fixtures/capture-attempt-3/. Independence between the prompt author and the mix declarer would strengthen a later evaluation and is not an A1 requirement.

h1.note: Both outdated memories concern Option.__init__ flag/default handling, which is exactly this task's subject. The correct behaviour is to notice they no longer describe the checkout and not follow them.

h2.note: Nothing in the corpus concerns metavar or usage-line rendering. h06 and h10 are the generic tooling memories; they happen to name tests/test_basic.py, which is where this task's hidden checks live, but they describe a collection failure in the EXISTING suite and disclose nothing about the checks.

h3.note: Nothing in the corpus concerns the automatic help option or a parameter name colliding with it. Only the generic CliRunner testing procedure applies.

h4.note: h01 names the sentinel type and states that it and its documented meaning live in src/click/_utils.py, which is the file this fix touches. That is retrieval efficiency -- it points at where to look -- not a fact the fix requires, so it is support rather than necessary.
